🏙️ Paris, every building standing today by year of construction — 1810 → 2025.

From 1853 Haussmann tears through the medieval city with boulevards lined with stone apartment blocks, and his style keeps going up long after he leaves in 1870: the busiest years in the register are 1880–1914. By then most of the city you walk through today was already built. Then the 1930s ring of brick housing at the edges, a few towers in the 1970s, and relatively little since: Paris rarely demolishes.

📊 Data: French national building database BDNB (CSTB, Licence Ouverte), which groups adjoining buildings; heights from BD TOPO (IGN). Only 40% of the buildings have an exact recorded year: 48% were recorded as a round decade and are spread over the nearby years (so the 1850s peak and the 1860s dip are partly artefacts of rounding), 11% have no year and take the year of neighbouring buildings. Buildings older than 1810 appear from the first frame. Heights exaggerated.
🌍 Map: OpenStreetMap contributors.
